title: Local presentability is invariant under categorical equivalence
statement: Use small colimits as defined in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and ordinary categories $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. A category is locally presentable relative to $\mathcal U$ if it has all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects such that every object is a $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of members of this family. A category is $\kappa$-filtered if each diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows admits a cocone, an object is $\kappa$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves these filtered colimits, and regular means that a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ still has cardinality less than $\kappa$. For every equivalence $E:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$, the category $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable relative to $\mathcal U$ if and only if $\mathcal D$ is locally presentable relative to $\mathcal U$.
